More accurate than a photo. Faster than typing.

Real chain nutrition, not a guess

A Whopper from MyFitnessPal is a generic 240 kcal patty. From VoCal it's the actual Burger King Whopper: 670 kcal, 28g protein, 49g carbs, 40g fat.

A coach that reads your day

App Intents for Log meal · Get daily macros · Open the mic. Works from Spotlight, Action Button, and Apple Watch.

Three seconds

From plate to log.

Three-tier resolution. Most of your queries never leave the device. The hard ones get the LLM. Either way you get real macros, not a guess.

  1. 01

    Tap the mic

    On-device SFSpeechRecognizer. The transcript appears live as you speak. No network round-trip for the recognition.

  2. 02

    We resolve it in three tiers

    Tier-0 on-device canon (<50ms for ~100 common foods). Tier-1 backend chain canon (~100ms for ~30 chains). Tier-2 Wafer GLM-5.1 + USDA fallback (3-7s for anything else).

  3. 03

    Logged. Synced. Done.

    Calorie ring updates, macros tick up, Apple Health gets the sample, Siri can read it back. The Coach reads your day's log when you ask what to eat next.

I've abandoned every calorie tracker in a week. VoCal is the first one where logging a Chipotle bowl is faster than ordering it.

Questions

The things people ask.

Cal AI needs you to take a photo. MyFitnessPal needs you to type and scroll. VoCal just needs you to speak. And VoCal actually knows the McDonald's, Starbucks, Chipotle, Chick-fil-A, Burger King, Subway, and Taco Bell menus by exact item — so "medium fry from McDonald's" resolves to the real 320 kcal, not a generic guess.

Yes for the common path. Speech recognition runs entirely on-device. The Tier-0 food canon (~100 most common foods) is bundled with the app — apple, banana, 8 oz chicken breast, slice of pizza all resolve with zero network. Chain queries and rare foods need a connection; if you're offline, an editorial fallback covers the killer demo phrases.

Audio is transcribed on-device via Apple's Speech framework and discarded immediately. Only the resulting transcript (e.g. "medium fry from McDonald's") leaves the device, and only when our chain canon or on-device cache misses. No audio is ever stored or used for advertising.

Every saved meal writes dietary energy, protein, carbs, and fat to HealthKit as a sample tagged "VoCal." Body fat % and body mass too, when you complete a body scan. You can mirror those into Apple Watch fitness rings, share with your doctor's app, or export the lot.

When the on-device cache and backend chain canon both miss, the request goes to Wafer Pass (GLM-5.1, JSON-mode, temp 0.1). OpenRouter (GPT-4o-mini) is the fallback if Wafer is down. USDA FoodData Central is the last structured fallback before a clearly-flagged generic estimate.
